[MUQATIL:17:16-18/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Whoever wants immediate worldly life receives whatever wealth God wills for whomever He chooses, then is sent to Hell, blamed by God and driven away.
[MUQATIL:17:16-18/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | The passage is said to have been revealed about three men from Thaqif, naming Farqad ibn Yamama, Abu Fatima ibn al-Bukhturi, and Safwan; the source then adds two unnamed placeholders.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p123/r8] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The one seeking only the immediate world is the idolater who does not believe in the Hereafter.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The one who receives what God wills of worldly benefit will still enter Hell amid God’s punishment.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | To be driven away means being banished far from Paradise and placed in Hell.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda glosses “blamed” as being in God’s punishment and “banished” as being in His torment.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r4] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | For one whose concern and pursuit are only worldly life, God hastens what He wills for whom He wills, then assigns Hell.
[FARRA:v2p119/r9] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد means that God gives from this-worldly provision to whomever He chooses.
[MAJAZ:v1p374/r2] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | مدحورا means expelled and removed; أدحر الشيطان means repel Satan, and the verbal noun is الدحور.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | The codex writes ما نشؤا with wāw after alif in Shuʿayb's verse, while the same form elsewhere lacks wāw, without a difference in meaning.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The worldly seeker works only for immediate life and lacks belief in resurrection or hope of divine reward or punishment; God gives such a person whatever worldly ease, hardship, or chastisement He wills, to whomever He wills.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | At the resurrection God sends this person to Hell, blamed for ingratitude and bad conduct toward prior favors and expelled far away.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda describes worldly life as the person's sole concern, aim, and intention, followed by being driven into Hell; the person is blamed amid God's favor and cast away amid His punishment.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو إسحاق الفزاري | reports | Abū Isḥāq explains “for whom We will” as meaning someone whose destruction God wills.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses مذموما as blameworthy or reproached.
[TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd explains العاجلة as the present world.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | العاجلة means this world; God hastens to a person who seeks it only what God wills, for whomever God wills, not whatever the person wills.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | Alternatively, the implied subject of نشاء is the servant: God gives the servant what he desires, if God wills it.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The threat of Hell follows because the person did not intend God through his deed.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | مذموما and مذءوما have the same meaning.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r6] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | مدحورا means driven far away from God's mercy; دحر means to drive someone away.
[NAHHAS:v2p419/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | God does not withhold the immediate world from one who does not seek the afterlife’s reward; He grants it to whom He wills.
[SULAMI:v1p384#5/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · الواسطي | reports | Al-Wasiti links renouncing the world with witnessing the afterlife, and says witnessing divine support erases self-regard while contemplating God's attributes makes servant attributes fall away.
[THALABI:v6p91/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The urgent life means this world; the adjective stands for “the urgent abode.” God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, whether abundance or restriction.
[THALABI:v6p91/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The worldly seeker eventually enters Hell, disgraced and expelled.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The verse parallels 3:145 about receiving a share of worldly reward. | mentions 3:145
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abū Isḥāq says such a person is put in Hell because he did not seek God through his deeds; madḥūr also means removed from God's mercy.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | Al-ʿājila is the present world, contrasted with the delayed Hereafter; worldly seekers receive only the amount God chooses for whom He chooses, not whatever they desire.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | This rebukes those who serve or profess Islam for worldly gain: many seeking it may fail, and whoever gets it receives only a divine allotment before entering Hell.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās glosses mazmūm as blameworthy and madḥūr as expelled or driven away.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | One who seeks worldly life through deeds, worship, or Islam receives only the amount God wills, and only for whom He wills.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Such a person enters Hell in the afterlife, blamed and banished for not intending God through his deeds.
[JISHUMI:v6p4177/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | “Condemned, expelled” is an adverbial state, while “knowing, seeing” is an accusative of specification or means “from one who knows.”
[JISHUMI:v6p4177/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | The promise about worldly seekers was revealed about emigrants seeking booty rather than God's reward.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Worldly seekers receive only what God wills, whether expansion, restriction, or destruction; afterward they enter Hell blamed and banished.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Those whose sole aim is this world, such as unbelievers and many sinners, receive only what God wills for whomever He chooses; both the grant and its recipient are restricted by divine choice.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Many people do not receive all they seek, while others are denied even the portion they desire, leaving them poor in both worlds.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The phrase for whom We will is an appositional subset of the preceding recipient, since the pronoun refers to people collectively.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r5] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | A reading has yashāʾ; if the pronoun refers to God, it has the same sense as the standard reading.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r6] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Alternatively the pronoun may refer to the servant, meaning the person receives the worldly things he wishes for, though God intends that grant for one of the many.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r7] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Another kind of worldly seeker performs afterlife deeds for worldly ends: hypocrisy, showing off, migration for gain or marriage, and fighting for spoils or fame.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r8] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A prophetic report says migration is valued according to its aim: migration to God and His Messenger is for them, while migration for a worldly prize is only for that prize.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r9] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Madḥūr means expelled from God's mercy.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The warning concerns one who wants only worldly life and believes in no afterlife; God grants only what He wills, then consigns all such unbelievers to Hell.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | On the reading with “We will,” the object may be what the seeker or God wishes; “for whom We will” qualifies both readings.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو إسحاق الفزاري | reports | Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī interprets “for whom We will” as “for one whose destruction We intend.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الجمهور | reports | Most read nashāʾ with nūn; Nāfiʿ also transmits yashāʾ with yāʾ.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Madḥūr means disgraced, expelled, humiliated, and subject to displeasure.
[TABRISI:17:18#2/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The immediate world is named for its short-lived quality; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills and may restrict the worldly seeker.
[TABRISI:17:18#2/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The worldly seeker enters Hell blamed and excluded from God's mercy.
[TABRISI:17:18/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Yuslīhā is circumstantial, and 'for whom We will' apposes the preceding clause; the pronoun repeats because the apposition is another clause.
[TABRISI:17:19-22/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Work done for worldly reward alone, without seeking God or the hereafter, earns only the worldly portion God wills and no afterlife reward; the gift may be misused and punished.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The one seeking the immediate world means a person whose deeds are aimed at worldly life; an adjective is used in place of the noun.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | The worldly provision hastened to such a person is explained either as worldly goods or as expansion and restriction of provision.

ZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو إسحاق الفزاري | reports | One interpretation of those chosen to receive hastened provision is that God intends their destruction.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Another interpretation is that God intends to hasten something for that person.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The passage rebukes people who work for worldly life: they obtain only what was allotted to them, then enter Hell in the afterlife.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن جرير | reports | Ibn Jarīr says this verse concerns those who do not believe in resurrection.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · القفال | reports | Al-Qaffal connects this verse to each person’s assigned “bird”: those seeking only worldly status may reject the prophets, yet receive only what God wills and end in Hell. | mentions 17:13
[RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Hell’s wording depicts punishment as lasting harm with humiliation and exile from divine mercy, without relief or escape.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Worldly success should not be mistaken for God’s approval: it may end in punishment, and a person’s deeds can drive them like an ill omen toward torment.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The phrase “for whom We will” warns that many who abandon religion for worldly gain obtain neither; they are the greatest losers despite thinking they act well. | mentions 18:104
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | He classifies actions by whether they aim at worldly good, afterlife good, both together, or neither; the verse directly treats the first two.
[QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The worldly seeker receives only what God wills, then faces accountability and Hell; hypocrites and show-offs who feign devotion for spoils gain no afterlife reward and receive only their allotted worldly share. | mentions 11:15, 11:16
[QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The wording refers to the immediate abode by its adjective; “rejected and banished” describes removal from God’s mercy.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The person seeking the immediate life has made it his sole concern.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Worldly grant is restricted by God’s will and choice, since no one receives every wish or all that they desire; this teaches that achievement and concern are gifts.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | In the phrase “and for whom We will,” the prepositional phrase substitutes for “to him” as a partitive apposition.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | A reading has “what He wills,” with the pronoun referring to God so it agrees with the common reading.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Another explanation takes “for whom” as a restriction to the person God specifically wills to grant.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | One reported interpretation applies the verse to hypocrites who joined Muslims in raids for a share of the spoils, not religious purpose.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The worldly seeker is cast into Hell, disgraced and driven away from God’s mercy.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The phrase for whom We wish is a partitive apposition to the preceding phrase, repeating its preposition; its pronoun refers to the person seeking this life.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God controls both what worldly benefit is accelerated and which seeker receives it; people may desire more than they receive, or be denied even what others obtain.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The pious believer chooses the wealth of the afterlife; worldly poverty may be better for that believer than receiving a worldly share.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The worldly seeker enters Hell in the afterlife, despised and expelled from God's mercy.
[QASHANI:17:18-21/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The worldly seeker has clouded readiness and dominant appetite; God hastens only the share decreed for whomever He wills, since desire alone cannot secure more than the allotment in the Preserved Tablet.
[QASHANI:17:18-21/r2] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Hell is the dark well of nature toward which the seeker inclines: its fire is deprivation, its verdict is blame among both worlds, and its state is expulsion from mercy.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The عاجلة is worldly life, and wanting it means preferring it over the afterlife; the omitted counterpart is that the worldly seeker acts for it while faith is absent. | mentions 17:19
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | Another view concerns people who use afterlife deeds for worldly gain, such as hypocrites, show-offs, migrants seeking worldly benefit, or fighters seeking booty and renown.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophetic report says that whoever migrates for a worldly prize or a woman has only the worldly object for which he migrated.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report warns that whoever seeks worldly gain through afterlife deeds receives no share in the afterlife.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | A reported occasion of revelation is hypocrites joining Muslim campaigns for booty rather than reward.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The conditional promise is limited twice: God hastens only what He wills and only for whom He wills, so worldly seekers do not necessarily obtain their wishes.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The majority read ما نشاء with first-person plural; a report from Nāfiʿ reads يشاء in third person, either as a shift referring to God or as referring to the conditional seeker, though not universally.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r17] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو إسحاق الفزاري | rejects | Al-Fazārī interprets لمن نريد as one whom God intends to destroy, but Abū Ḥayyān says the wording does not support this.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | جعلنا means made: Hell is the first object and its second complement is implied by the construction, yielding Hell as the unbelievers’ destination; another grammarian supplies an omitted second object meaning destination or recompense.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | مذموما signals humiliation, while مدحورا signals distance and expulsion from God’s mercy.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | من is conditional, عجلنا its answer, ما يشاء its object, and لمن نريد a partitive apposition from له with the governor repeated.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | جعل is causative here; يصلاها is circumstantial from either له or جهنم, and مذموما is circumstantial from the subject of يصلاها.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · قيل | reports | An omitted contrasting condition is understood: the one who wants the immediate life also strives for it while being an unbeliever, as the following context indicates.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, the intended person wants worldly life through deeds directed toward the Hereafter, like a hypocrite.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Not everyone who seeks worldly pleasure receives it; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, qualifying other verses that state the promise more generally.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The worldly seeker who is assigned Hell enters it engulfed on every side, blamed for choosing the fleeting over the lasting and cast away in humiliation.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عائشة | reports | A report from ʿAisha calls this world the home of one without a home and the wealth of one without wealth, gathered by one lacking reason.
[BURHAN:v2p129/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The hadith that actions depend on intentions has an explicit Quranic basis in the contrast between seeking the immediate world and the Hereafter, and in accountability for what hearts intend and oaths they bind.
[BURHAN:v2p16/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | When people who pursue the world receive little, the answer is that God grants the immediate world only as much as He wills and to whom He wills.
[NASHR:v1p290/r1] NASHR, d. 833 · عامة أهل الأداء | holds | Most performance authorities assimilate the adjacent sounds in this locus; this is the practice across Ibn Farḥ’s routes from al-Dūrī and Ibn Jarīr’s routes from al-Sūsī and was read by al-Dānī and his students.
[NASHR:v1p290/r2] NASHR, d. 833 · جميع العراقيين | reports | All Iraqi transmitters use izhār through every route of Abū al-Zarʿāʾ from al-Dūrī and every route of al-Sūsī; the author accepts both assimilation and izhār.
[NASHR:v1p290/r5] NASHR, d. 833 · القاسم بن عبد الوارث وصاحب التجريد | reports | Al-Dūrī via al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith transmits assimilation in فلا جناح عليه, المسيح عيسى, and الريح عاصفة; al-Tajrīd reports it from Shuʿja and ʿUbayd Allāh in فلا جناح and المسيح. | mentions 2:158, 3:45, 21:81

r | holds | Dāl assimilates into ten following letters regardless of its vowel, except an open dāl preceded by a consonant assimilates only into tāʾ; dāl into tāʾ assimilates in every case because the letters share an articulation point.

[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | A person seeking only the immediate world receives some, not all, of what God wills for selected people; the outcome depends on divine power rather than the seeker's strength.

[DURR-FULL:v5p254/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الضحاك | reports | The seeker of the immediate world is one who does deeds intending worldly gain; God hastens what He wills for whom He wills.
[DURR-FULL:v5p254/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | The immediate-world seeker makes it his concern, desire, request, and intention; God gives what He wills, then consigns him to Hell, disgraced under divine wrath and expelled into punishment.
